subject: Data handling & proof-of-erasure questions for EU residency and backups
messages:
From: Elena Morales <privacy@aurorahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Kelly <peter.kelly@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T09:14:00+00:00
Subject: Questions on erasure requirements and backups (DPA redlines)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. We had a quick pass and our legal/privacy team surfaced two areas we need clarity on before we can sign:

1) Erasure scope: The redline requires deletion of customer data within 30 days of termination. Our main question is whether that 30-day window applies to all persistent backups and snapshots (including cross-region disaster recovery copies) or strictly to production datasets.

2) Evidence of erasure: For regulators we need an auditable proof-of-erasure artifact. Would Redwood be able to provide a certificate or report showing deletion operations (timestamps, affected datasets, and per-region execution) for a given account? If so, what format and retention duration for those certificates do you support?

I've attached our annotated redlines (aurora-dpa-redlines.docx).

Appreciate a short call if that's easier — we can do 30 minutes this week.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Morales
Senior Privacy Counsel, Aurora Health
privacy@aurorahealth.com
+44 20 7946 0123

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <privacy@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T11:02:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Questions on erasure requirements and backups (DPA redlines)

Hi Elena,

Thanks — we got the redlines. Quick summary up-front: we can meet the 30-day erase window for production data and provide an auditable erasure report; backups and cross-region DR have a slightly different operational model that we need to clarify and possibly carve out with alternative controls.

I've looped in Marcus (Legal) and propose a short runbook of what we can commit to:
- Production dataset deletion within 30 days of termination, including KV caches and prefix caches.
- Rolling snapshot/backups: full immutable backups used for DR are retained per configured retention windows; we can commit to a guaranteed remove-from-live-access and a logical deletion marker within 30 days, with physical media/replica purge subject to backup rotation cycles (typically 90 days).
- We can produce an "erasure certificate" (PDF) containing account id, deletion timestamp(s), list of affected storage pools, and the operator/automation job id.

Marcus — can you confirm legal OK with offering the logical-deletion + backup-rotation carve (and whether we should offer a shorter rotation window for Aurora as a paid option)?

Elena — happy to take a 30-minute call; I'm free tomorrow 14:00-15:00 UTC.

Thanks,
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <privacy@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T08:21:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Questions on erasure requirements and backups (DPA redlines)

Sofia — filing a short legal position: we are comfortable with the approach Sofia outlined subject to two items being captured in the contract. Please propose language similar to the following: 

1) Production Data Erasure: "Redwood will permanently delete Customer Production Data within thirty (30) days after termination of Services and provide a written certificate of erasure."

2) Backups and Disaster Recovery: "For Backup Copies and Disaster Recovery Replicas, Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to logically delete Customer Data within thirty (30) days of termination. Physical deletion from immutable backup media will occur in accordance with Redwood's backup rotation schedule (not to exceed ninety (90) days) unless Customer elects and pays for accelerated media purging. Redwood will document the deletion actions and provide evidentiary logs upon reasonable request."

3) Audit Evidence Format: we can provide a PDF certificate plus a structured CSV export of deletion events (UTC timestamps, storage pool id, operator id, and job id). We prefer to keep raw audit logs internal but will provide the structured export under NDA where required.

Naomi — please confirm the engineering/ops feasibility and typical timelines.

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <privacy@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T10:46:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Questions on erasure requirements and backups (DPA redlines)

Thanks Marcus — engineering confirms this is operationally feasible. Implementation notes: 

- Logical deletion (remove from active indexes, zero-out object metadata pointers) can be executed within 48 hours of the erase job kicking off; that will render data inaccessible to all live services.
- Immutable snapshots are retained per backup policy; we can run a media-purge job to excise snapshots that contain only Aurora data, but that requires a scheduled maintenance window and coordination (we normally batch these monthly). Typical completion for an accelerated purge is within 5–10 business days after scheduling.
- We can generate the certificate PDF and the CSV event export automatically from the erasure orchestration system; the CSV will include timestamp, storage region, storage pool id, job id, and a hash-of-deletion-manifest for verification. We suggest the CSV be provided via a secure S3 presigned URL (7-day expiry) or delivered in the DocuSign envelope if preferred.

Attachments: redwood-erasure-playbook.pdf (operator runbook — redacted).

Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Elena Morales <privacy@aurorahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Peter Kelly <peter.kelly@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-24T16:33:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Questions on erasure requirements and backups (DPA redlines)

Sofia/Marcus/Naomi — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of follow-ups before we close this section of the DPA: 

- For the audit CSV, can Redwood include the operator automation job id as a UUID and sign the manifest hash (PGP or equivalent) so we have tamper-evident evidence?
- For cross-border admin access: please confirm whether any Redwood support engineers outside the EEA might need to access deleted-data artifacts during the purge window, and if so what role-based access controls and logging you apply.

If those two points are acceptable we'll prepare a final redline. We can accept the backup rotation carve as long as the accelerated purge option is available for our account (we're open to discussing cost).

Would you like me to upload the updated redline back to the HubSpot deal (I can) or shall I wait for the DocuSign envelope?

Best regards,
Elena
